g.text: Wasan mathematicians — reading lines of transmission
Arrows show sourced teacher–student links, not merely a shared subject.
A selected line within the Seki school
Araki Murahide → Matsunaga Yoshisuke → Yamaji Nushizumi → Ajima Naonobu
Matsunaga: birth uncertain–1744 (c. 1690 also given); Ajima: 1732–1798 (sources differ)
Sources: biographical dictionaries and National Diet Library authority records
Yamaji learned from more than one mathematician
Nakane Genkei → Yamaji Nushizumi / Kurushima Yoshihiro → Yamaji Nushizumi
Yamaji Nushizumi → Fujita Sadasuke (1734–1807)
Kurushima: Yoshihiro; died late 1757 (January 1758 Gregorian). Source: dictionary records
Ishiguro Nobuyoshi (1760–1836): three fields of study
Nakada Takahiro → Ishiguro Nobuyoshi [mathematics]
Miyai Yasutai → Ishiguro Nobuyoshi [surveying]
Nishimura Taichu → Ishiguro Nobuyoshi [astronomy and calendars]
Source: Agency for Cultural Affairs, guide to the Ishiguro materials
Research fields and transmission require different diagrams
Tanaka Yoshizane (1651–1719): elimination, determinants, magic squares; not Ishiguro’s teacher
Yamaji Yukiharu: Nushizumi’s son; astronomy and mathematics. Source: University of Tokyo
Seki’s study with Takahara Yoshitane is tradition, not a confirmed direct link
Not a complete lineage or licensing chart. See the article for variant dates and readings.
AI NOBORU | Updated 15 September 2026 | Sources and variants appear in the article
